note: Each item says what it does, why, Microsoft's page for it, and how it is undone. 'registry' items are undone from the before-state each run saves; 'handler' items name a function in scripts/settings/Set-Baseline.ps1 that saves and restores its own state. HKCU items apply to the signed-in person who runs the script.

items.title: Turn on restore points
items.what: Turns on System Protection for the Windows drive so Windows keeps restore points.
items.why: A restore point lets the PC go back to how it was before a bad update, driver or app, and deskside makes one before every change it makes.
items.undo: Turns System Protection back off for the Windows drive if it was off before.

items.title: Block potentially unwanted apps
items.what: Turns on Microsoft Defender's blocking of potentially unwanted apps (adware, bundled toolbars, junk 'cleaners').
items.why: Most junk on family PCs arrives bundled with free downloads; this stops it at install time.
items.undo: Sets the PUA protection setting back to its previous value.

items.title: SmartScreen on for apps and files
items.what: Turns SmartScreen's check of downloaded apps and files back on when it has been switched off.
items.why: SmartScreen warns before running unknown or known-bad downloads, a common way scams start.

items.title: Warn before update restarts
items.what: Turns on 'Notify me when a restart is required to finish updating' in Windows Update.
items.why: The PC tells the person before it restarts for updates, so they aren't surprised and don't lose work.
items.undo: Puts the previous value back (or removes it if it wasn't set).

items.title: Show file name extensions
items.what: Shows the ending of file names (.pdf, .exe) in File Explorer.
items.why: A file called invoice.pdf.exe looks like a PDF when extensions are hidden; showing them makes fake files easy to spot.

items.title: Turn on Storage Sense
items.what: Lets Windows clear temporary files and old Recycle Bin items automatically when the disk runs low.
items.why: A full disk is one of the most common reasons a family PC becomes slow or stops updating.

items.title: Turn off ads and tips
items.what: Turns off suggested apps and ads in Start, tips and 'fun facts' on the lock screen, suggested content in Settings, the 'finish setting up your device' nag and tailored offers.
items.why: These prompts push sign-ups and installs that confuse people who don't know they can say no.
items.undo: Puts each previous value back (or removes it if it wasn't set).
